## Summary

P0.06 — the **sandbox side of the run model**: the `Engine` abstraction and its `AgentSdkEngine`, the two-uid `apps/run-task` image, the SDK→event mapper with recorded fixtures, `FakeEngine`, `ManagedAgentsEngine`, and input-scoped subagents. Stacked on P0.05 (boundary hooks). Implements spec §12.2 / §12.4 step 4 / §12.5 / §12.6 / §13.5.

The whole engine is **dependency-injected** so it is fully unit-testable with recorded fixtures and no Agent SDK, no AWS, no network — and the two privilege-separation ACs are proven at the **real kernel level** via a purpose-built Docker image.

## What changed

**`packages/engine`** (new): `Engine` interface (`startPhase`/`abort`/`usage`); `AgentSdkEngine` building the §12.2 `query()` options verbatim (scrubbed env, `dontAsk`, cosmetic `disallowedTools`, per-phase `maxBudgetUsd`/`maxTurns`, subagent depth 1 / ≤5, 1-h caching, OTel, S3 sessionStore, abortController, the PreToolUse hook); `ManagedAgentsEngine` stub passing the same conformance suite (REQ-ARCH-7); `FakeEngine` replaying recorded fixtures (G21); the SDK→event **mapper** (`src/mapper/`) with 8 recorded fixtures; the subagent roster; input-scoped subagent launch specs; OTel config (content flags off).

**`apps/run-task`**: the two-uid image contract — `Dockerfile` (ARM64, two uids, harness-only secrets, read-only rootfs + tmpfs, `setpriv` drop, `unshare` scoped runner); `bootstrap.ts` (harness→agent launch, scrubbed env); `secrets.ts` (harness-only secrets file); the Unix-socket **hook daemon** + client (`@rhema/hooks` decisions cross the socket, the token/audit/control never do); the per-request proxy-credential injector + reference validation rule; `docker/privsep-check.sh` + `Dockerfile.privsep-test` (kernel AC1/AC4 proof).

## Design decisions

- **DI everywhere.** The vendored SDK is injected as a `QueryFn`; both engines route their message stream through the one mapper, which is exactly why both pass the same conformance suite. The live SDK adapter is a one-liner deferred to dev (D-P0.06-4).
- **The mapper is the single choke point** for the visibility split: every event is built via `parseRunEvent` (whitelist) with its catalogue visibility, `agent.note` only from `@rhema/contracts` templates, and `source.read` URLs read *only* from a structured tool-result field — never scanned out of page body text.
- **`usage.tick` split:** the mapper emits a token-level `usage` marker per turn; the credit-bearing `usage.tick` event is the orchestrator's (it owns the cap + proxy rate table) — §12.4 step 6.
- **Kernel-level proof.** AC1 (uid `agent` denied the secrets file) and AC4 (scoped mount namespace = exactly the enumerated files, out-of-set read fails at the kernel) are verified by building and running a Docker image with `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` — not just unit-mocked.
- **Slim base stand-in** for the distroless target (hardening deferred, D-P0.06-3): `node:22-bookworm-slim` + util-linux so the `setpriv`/`unshare`/`mount` mechanics actually run in Phase 0.
